chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿUbaydī, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who enters janabah while traveling and finds nothing except snow or frozen water. He said: “He is in the position of necessity; he performs tayammum, and I do not think that he should return to this land which destroys his religion.”
So the correct understanding of this report is that when he is unable to use it because of cold or something else, that is indicated by what he narrated:

key_terms.الثَّلْجَ: snow, the only available form of water mentioned here
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, the state in which the ruling is being discussed
key_terms.الضَّرُورَةِ: necessity, the condition that permits an exceptional ruling
key_terms.دِينَهُ: his religion, referring to the risk or hardship affecting religious practice
key_terms.مَاءً جَامِدًا: frozen water that cannot be normally used
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum as a substitute for purification with water
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: enters the state of janabah requiring ghusl

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a traveler in janabah finds only snow or frozen water and cannot use it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a traveler who enters janabah and cannot use available frozen water or snow due to necessity. In such a case, the ruling is tayammum, showing the accommodation in the Shariah when the use of water is not practically possible or harmful.
